catalog_quote: The present chapter is based on previous work as well as my own fieldwork on the Harakmbut language, both of which focus on the Amarakaeri/Arakmbut dialect, which has the highest number of speakers. ... Detailed studies on the dialectal differences are lacking, but the dialects are reported to be mutually intelligible. ... The domain of stress assignment in a phonological word differs according to word class. For nouns, the stress domain is the root plus derivational affixes; the main stress falls on the penultimate syllable. ... As shown in (3) and (5c), inflectional suffixes like case endings do not bear on stress assignment. By contrast, derivational suffixes attaching to nouns typically affect stress placement (5). ... audit.recode_to: Penultimate stress (default) within a morphologically delimited domain: certain final suffixes/syllables (-ta, -nda, -na, ne, -a 'et al.') fall outside it, giving surface antepenult — i.e. the same MORPHOLOGICAL/penult-in-stem-domain type already coded for amar1274, now on huac1244's own evidence (Peck 1979 [2008]: 27, Toyeri and Sapiteri dialects). Carry cautions: author calls the suprasegmentals 'no resueltos', verbs with suffix strings 'más compleja', all stressed vowels long and no stress minimal pairs; Pittman (unpublished, Huachipaeri proper) held stress non-phonemic and predictable from vowel length. Evidence grade: primary preliminary phonology sketch (1956-57 fieldwork), not open-text/undetermined.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every fragment of the deciding Van linden 2023 quotation is verbatim in the held postprint text at the stated pages (3, 4, 7, 29). (2) Deciding source: a 2023 handbook sketch of the sister language Arakmbut (amar1274) that explicitly excludes Watipaeri; the record was left UNDETERMINED solely because the Huachipaeri-side primaries were unreachable on 12 Sep (Cloudflare on sil.org, PuRe 401, no Wayback). Glottolog lists exactly two phonology items for huac1244: Peck 2008 [1979] (MED, 104 pp) and van den Eynde 1972 (43 pp). (3) I located an open archive. VII.A 'Acento' p. 27 states penultimate stress in most polysyllables with antepenult in words

sources.citation: Peck, Charles. 2008 [1979; typescript dated marzo 1958]. Toyeri y Sapiteri: un informe preliminar de la fonología y el vocabulario. Datos Etno-Lingüísticos 67. Lima: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 106 PDF pp. CC BY-NC-ND 3.0. Open copy: archive.org item 'toyerisapiteridiccionario' (same work as sil.org reapdata / MPG PuRe item_406820).
sources.quote: p. 27: 'Los detalles suprasegmentales de acento y la duración de vocales no se han resuelto. Las observaciones generales que siguen son basadas en la mayor parte, en enunciaciones cortas pedidas. VII.A. ACENTO. En la mayoría de las palabras que tienen dos o más sílabas el acento se encuentra en la penúltima sílaba. Las excepciones son palabras que terminan con ciertas sílabas, tales como (-ta), (-nda) o (-na), (ne), (-a), et al., en las cuales se pone el acento sobre la antepenúltima sílaba. En aisladas respuestas pedidas con los sufijos arriba se han observado algunas variaciones en la coloca
